806: | Error injection | ≤ 600 tokens per event | per signature per session |
807: | Risky-action injection | ≤ 800 tokens per event | per claim per session |
808: | Déjà-vu alert | ≤ 300 tokens | per claim per session |
809: | Per-session push cap | 20k tokens total | n/a |
810: | Claim index, read by the agent itself | ≤ 1.5k tokens per subsystem | n/a (pull) |
811: | MCP tool schemas (standing cost) | Measured, reported (§10.4) | n/a |
812: 
813: MCP tool descriptions are listed in the system prompt of every session and count against Antigravity's customization budget, not the rules budget. Their size is measured and reported rather than guessed. Descriptions are kept terse.
814: 
815: A per-session **delivery ledger** records every claim delivered, so delivery is never repeated and the metrics in §10 can be computed.
816: 
817: **Rendering.** In the task brief and in touch, error and risky-action injections, each claim is one line with three parts:
818: 
819: 1. its `apply` line, or its title if it has none;
820: 2. its ID;
821: 3. a stamp saying how current it is: `verified 2026-09-24 @69d9c813`, `open as of 2026-09-30`, or the `suspect` or `conditions-changed` marker.
822: 
823: Before injecting, the hook checks that each claim's anchored files still exist. That is a file-system check, well within §7.8. A missing file renders the claim as `suspect` even if the tick hasn't re-checked it yet. The plugin's rules file tells the agent once that memory reflects the stamped point in time, and that it should check named files and symbols before relying on them.
824: 
825: ### 7.2 Task start
826: 
827: 1. Always-on: `MAP.md`, loaded by the harness's own instruction file. The repo's root `AGENTS.md` (Antigravity) and `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code) each include it: `@[memory map](.memory/views/MAP.md)` and `@.memory/views/MAP.md` respectively. This costs ~2k of the 20k rules budget and is cached with the system prompt. Fallback, if include semantics don't work as expected (P0 experiment E2): inject at `PreInvocation` with `invocationNum == 0`.
828: 2. At the first model invocation, the delivery hook reads the task text (first user message) and branch from the transcript.
829: 3. The hook links the task to entities using the local index:
830:    - lexical match on entity names, paths, symbols and error strings;
831:    - plus files already open or mentioned;
832:    - if lexical matching yields nothing, the hook injects the map-level summary with a one-line pointer to the claim indexes (§5.5), so the agent can choose the relevant subsystems itself at once. It also spools a brief request. The next tick prepares the brief in a housekeeping run, and the next `PreInvocation` picks it up from `alerts/` (typically within ~75 s). If it needs the brief sooner, the agent can call `memory.brief` synchronously (~13 s). An LLM is never called inside a hook.
833: 4. It renders the **task brief**, in priority order:
834:    1. invariants of the involved subsystems;
835:    2. open issues and in-flight work;
836:    3. ruled-out approaches;
837:    4. relevant procedures;
838:    5. decisions.
839: 5. The agent can call `memory.brief(task)` later to refresh it when the task direction changes.
840: 
841: ### 7.3 File touch
842: 
843: When the agent reads or edits a file whose entities (file, symbols, subsystem) have pushable claims not yet delivered this session, inject:
844: 
845: - `invariant`, `ruled-out`, `fact` and `open-issue` claims for those entities, most specific anchor first;
846: - one line per claim, rendered as in §7.1 (`apply` line, ID and currency stamp). The agent can call `memory.why(<id>)` for evidence.
847: 
848: ### 7.4 Error
849: 
850: When a tool outcome (command, test, device) contains text matching a `failure-signature` `match` block, inject the signature's cause and fix before the agent's next reasoning step. Matching is deterministic (string and regex on the ledger excerpt).
851: 
852: ### 7.5 Risky action
853: 
854: Default risky actions (configurable):
855: 
856: - flash, monitor and OTA upload tools;
857: - release scripts;
858: - edits to `sdkconfig*`, `platformio.ini`, `dependencies.lock` or partition tables;
859: - dependency upgrades.
860: 
861: **Timing constraint.** `PreInvocation` runs before the model decides what to do, so it can't see a concrete action until after that action has run. The only event between a proposed action and its execution is `PreToolUse`, and it can't inject context. It can return `deny` or `ask` with a `reason`, which the agent (or user) sees.
862: 
863: **Delivery modes** (per pattern, in `config.yaml`):
864: 
865: | Mode | Behaviour | Default for |
866: |---|---|---|
867: | `gate-once` | At `PreToolUse`, if the relevant `procedure`/`invariant` claims haven't been delivered this session, return `deny` with a reason containing them (≤ 800 tokens) and an explicit "re-issue the call to proceed". The ledger marks them delivered, so the re-issued call is allowed. Costs one extra round-trip, once per session per claim set. | Flash, release, partition-table edits |
868: | `ask` | At `PreToolUse`, return `ask` with the claims as the reason, so the user decides. | Off by default; for teams that want a human in the loop |
869: | `next-invocation` | Allow the call; queue the claims for the next `PreInvocation`. No extra round-trip, but delivery comes after the action. | sdkconfig and dependency edits |
870: | `anticipate` | Inject at `PreInvocation` when the transcript suggests the action is imminent (e.g. a successful build in a session that has flashed before). | Optional addition to any mode |
871: 
872: This must coexist with existing gates such as esp32-app-foundation's `flash-tag-gate.py`. Hooks for the same event run in sequence; a `deny` from either stops the call.
873: 
874: ### 7.6 Déjà-vu alerts (optional, warm path)
875: 
876: The main defence against repeating a dead-end is not an alert at all:
877: 
878: - **Tier 0: proactive delivery (primary).** Ruled-out approaches for an entity are delivered in the task brief (§7.2) and on first touch of that entity (§7.3), before any plan to retry exists. Most prevention happens here.
879: - **Tier 1: lexical safety net.** It catches a concrete retry as it is proposed.
880: - **Tier 2: late correction.** On Antigravity it arrives about a minute behind, so it corrects the *next* attempt rather than preventing the first. On Claude Code it arrives in seconds through `asyncRewake` (§12.2).
881: 
882: **Tier 1: lexical (no LLM).**
883: 
884: - Every `ruled-out` claim carries a `match` block, generated at extraction from the failed attempts' concrete commands, config keys, symbols and values (§6.5, rule 9). Example: `any: ["vTaskDelay", "INT_WDT_TIMEOUT", "CHECK_CPU1"]` scoped to the entities `BLEStack::init` and `NimBLEDevice::init`.
885: - A match requires two conditions:
886:   1. an anchored entity is in play in the session (touched or mentioned);
887:   2. the claim's `match` terms appear in the text being checked.
888: - **At `PreToolUse`**, the hook checks the concrete proposed command or edit. A match against a `verified` or stronger `ruled-out` claim uses `gate-once`: `deny` with "This was tried on <date> and failed because <reason> (clm-…). If your approach differs, re-issue the call." This is the only way to catch the retry *before* it runs.
889: - **At `PreInvocation`**, the hook checks the latest reasoning in the transcript tail. A match queues a ≤ 300-token alert for this invocation. This catches plans that haven't turned into a tool call yet.
890: 
891: **Tier 2: semantic (housekeeping run on the next tick; on Claude Code, an `asyncRewake` hook).**
892: 
893: - At `PreInvocation`, if new reasoning mentions an entity with `ruled-out` claims and tier 1 didn't fire, the hook spools a request.
894: - The next tick asks a small model whether the plan is substantively the same as a ruled-out approach. It batches all pending requests into one call.
895: - On a match, it writes an alert to `alerts/<conversation-id>/`. The next `PreInvocation` delivers it: "You're about to retry X. It failed on <date> because Y (clm-…)."
896: - On Antigravity, latency is up to about a minute plus the call time. In a fast debugging session the agent may already be committed to the first retry by then, so treat tier 2 as a correction for the *next* attempt. It can still stop the second and third retries, which is where the 22 September BLE session lost most of its time.
897: - **[R2]** On Claude Code, a `PostToolBatch` hook spools the request and starts an `asyncRewake` hook that runs the check at once. On a match it exits with code 2, and Claude is woken with the alert as a system reminder within seconds.
898: - Each check is an interactive small call dominated by fixed overhead (§4.4.1). All pending checks are batched into one call per tick, and there are per-day caps.
899: - Requests are rate-limited per conversation (default: at most one in flight, at most one per 5 model calls).
900: - Default: enabled for `ruled-out` claims with status `verified` or higher only.
901: 
902: ### 7.7 Pull tools
903: 
904: | Tool | Returns |
905: |---|---|
906: | `memory.ask(question)` | Answer synthesised from claims, with claim IDs; falls back to episode search with explicit "unverified" marking |
907: | `memory.why(target)` | For a file, symbol, config key or claim ID: decisions and invariants plus evidence chain (claim → episodes → commits) |
908: | `memory.history(entity)` | Chronological claim and supersession history for an entity |
909: | `memory.brief(task)` | Regenerated task brief |
910: | `memory.note(text)` | Lets the agent or user flag something explicitly. Recorded as an event with `provenance: agent-note` or `human`, reconciled like any other candidate. This is optional and costs the working agent a single short tool call. |
911: | `memory.stats()` | Observability summary (§10.4): claim counts by type, status and subsystem; delivery and hit-rate figures for recent sessions; pipeline cost; coverage gaps |
912: 
913: All six tools ship from the start. Their use is instrumented (§10.4), so trimming or merging tools later is a data-driven decision.
914: 
915: ### 7.8 Performance
916: 
917: Antigravity hooks run synchronously and block the agent loop, and `PreInvocation` runs before *every* model call. Latency therefore adds up: at 100 ms per call, a session with 300 model calls gains 30 s.
918: 
919: - **Delivery hook fast path.** Check the conversation's `alerts/` directory and read the transcript from the last cursor (tail only). If nothing new matches, exit. Target: p95 ≤ 60 ms, p50 ≤ 30 ms.
920: - **Delivery hook with injection.** Local SQLite read-only queries plus formatting. Target: p95 ≤ 150 ms.
921: - **Implementation.** Hooks run the compiled Go binary (§18), so start-up costs milliseconds. E5 confirms the fast-path budget on macOS and Windows.
922: - **Measurement.** Cumulative hook time per session is recorded (§10.4) and reported against a session budget (default ≤ 2% of wall-clock time).
923: - **Failure behaviour.** No LLM calls and no network in hooks. If the index is missing or locked, the hook exits with an empty injection. Memory must never block or break work.
924: 
925: ### 7.9 Degraded modes
926: 
927: | Level | Condition | What still works |
928: |---|---|---|
929: | **Full** | Sidecars running, index current | Everything |
930: | **No ticks** | Scheduled sidecar not running (Antigravity closed, sidecars disabled, machine without Antigravity and no OS schedule) | Capture (`Stop` copies transcripts), delivery from the last index, déjà-vu tier 1, pull tools (`ask`/`brief` synthesis still runs synchronously). Spooled work waits for the next tick. |
931: | **No housekeeping** | `agy` missing, signed out, or quota exhausted | Capture, delivery and pull tools that don't need synthesis. LLM jobs stay queued; the circuit breaker stops retries until `agy` works again. |
932: | **No index** | Index missing or corrupt | Map via the `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` include; the agent can walk MAP → claim index → claim files (§5.5); pull tools fall back to text search over `.memory/views/` and claim files; hooks no-op. The index can be rebuilt with `repo-memory reindex`. |
933: | **Native floor** | No hooks and no tick (e.g. a harness where the plugin's hooks are disabled) | The always-on map include; generated path-scoped subsystem rules (`.claude/rules/` with `paths:` on Claude Code; Glob rules on Antigravity, pending E4/C6); MCP pull tools over the last index |
934: | **Plugin off** | Plugin disabled or not installed (e.g. a collaborator) | `.memory/views/*.md` and claim files remain readable Markdown in the repo; the map include still loads if present, and any agent can follow it to the claim indexes |

938: ## 8. Validity and re-checking
939: 
940: Re-checks are triggered by dependency changes, never by time or disuse.
941: 
942: | Change detected | Claims affected | Action |
943: |---|---|---|
944: | Merge to main changes a file | Claims anchored to changed symbols or windows (fingerprint mismatch) | Set `suspect`; queue a behavioural verify; on pass, clear and restamp `verified_at`; on fail, send to Reconcile with the diff as evidence |
945: | Symbol or file deleted or renamed | Claims anchored to it | Attempt re-anchor (rename detection); else `needs-review` |
946: | `dependencies.lock` / `platformio.ini` / SDK version change | Claims whose `conditions` reference the changed item | Set `conditions-changed`; `ruled-out` claims are delivered as "may work now" |
947: | sdkconfig value change | Claims anchored to that config key | Set `suspect`; verify |
948: | Revert on main | Claims with the reverted commit as evidence | Re-evaluate |
949: | A closure condition fires: issue closed, branch merged, work order complete, or a later episode shows the success outcome | `open-issue` claims whose `closes_when` lists it (§5.3.1) | Set `resolved`, with the closing event as evidence. If a fixing episode exists, its own extraction may yield a `failure-signature` or `decision`. |
950: | Human correction | The named claim | Apply as a `confirmed` or `refuted` event |
951: 
952: **Evaluating closure conditions.** Branches and PA work orders are checked every tick (local git and PA ledger reads). Outcome conditions are checked as each new episode is processed. Issue state needs the network, so it is checked at most daily through the git host's CLI.
953: 
954: **Explicitly out of scope:** decay by age, decay by retrieval frequency, and confidence scores that change with use. A claim about a subsystem nobody has touched in a year is as valid as the day it was verified, because nothing it depends on has changed. `open-issue` claims are no exception: they close on events, not with age.

958: ## 9. Coverage and elicitation
959: 
960: ### 9.1 Coverage model
961: 
962: For each subsystem, the pipeline computes a coverage record:
963: 
964: | Dimension | Measure |
965: |---|---|
966: | Rationale | Number of `decision` claims vs. key design points (public interfaces, major files) |
967: | Invariants | Number of `invariant` claims and the share enforced by a test or gate |
968: | Verification | Presence of at least one `procedure` for testing or verifying the subsystem |
969: | Failure knowledge | `failure-signature` and `ruled-out` counts relative to churn and incident history |
970: | Freshness | Share of claims that are `suspect` or `conditions-changed`, and `open-issue` claims with `closes_when: unknown` |
971: | Referenced gaps | `gaps` reported by extraction (§6.5) for the subsystem and not yet covered by a claim, counted by how many episodes mention each |
972: 
973: **Gap score** = churn (commits in last 90 days) × complexity × (1 − coverage). Frequently referenced gaps are also candidates for elicitation questions (§9.2).
974: 
975: ### 9.2 Elicitation
976: 
977: - Weekly (configurable), the tick picks **1–3 targeted questions** for the highest gap scores. For example: "Why does DataManager use FetchContext deadlines rather than per-source timeouts?"
978: - Questions go into the weekly **review report**, an IDE-visible conversation (§4.4), never into a working session.
979: - The human answers in that conversation. The sweep captures the conversation, and the human's messages become `human_answers` events, which become `confirmed` claims. The report's own text is never treated as evidence.
980: - The questions are also written to a `QUESTIONS.md` view, so they can be answered later or by someone else.
981: 
982: #### 9.2.1 Reading replies from report conversations
983: 
984: Report conversations mix three kinds of text: the automated kickoff prompt, the report agent's generated text (derived from memory), and the human's replies. Only the last is evidence. The mechanism must not depend on an LLM guessing who said what:
985: 
986: 1. **Record what was asked.** When the tick starts a report, the job table records the conversation ID, the kickoff prompt's hash, and the question IDs and claim IDs presented (e.g. `Q-017`, `clm-…`).
987: 2. **Classify authors structurally.** Author classification (§5.1) uses the harness's own message roles, excluding the kickoff prompt. The report agent's text counts as an exposure to every claim it presented, so nothing it says can support those claims (P13).
988: 3. **Parse explicit commands mechanically, without an LLM,** from human-authored steps: `approve clm-…`, `reject clm-…`, `approve all <subsystem>`, and `Q-017: <answer>`. These become review events and `human_answers` events directly.
989: 4. **Interpret free-text replies conservatively.** A small model maps each reply to the question or claim IDs it addresses. The human's verbatim text is stored as the evidence.
990:    - A resulting claim is `confirmed` only if the reconciler finds the human's text states the fact explicitly.
991:    - Otherwise it is `needs-review`. The next report quotes the interpretation back for confirmation: "I understood X from your answer to Q-017. Correct?"
992: 5. **Give the report agent no memory-write tools.** It is instructed to present questions verbatim and never answer on the human's behalf. Anything it types is excluded structurally in any case.
993: 
994: ### 9.3 Inferred backfill
995: 
996: For subsystems with no rationale coverage, a one-off pass infers `decision` claims from code, commit messages and PR descriptions. These claims have status `hypothesis` and are tagged `inferred`. They're shown in views as "inferred, unconfirmed" and are never pushed until a human confirms them.
997: 
998: ### 9.4 Invariant enforcement
999: 
1000: Each `invariant` claim may carry `enforced_by: <test|lint|gate path>`. Unenforced invariants in high-churn subsystems are listed as **proposed work** in the weekly review report, for example "turn this invariant into a CI check". The memory system never changes code itself (§4.4). The human, a PA project or the bug-fixer loop picks up the work in an IDE session. Enforced invariants are re-checked by CI, not only by the pipeline.
1001: 
1002: Other proposals raised the same way include human-facing docs that contradict verified claims, and stale `framework-expert` skill sections.

1006: ## 10. Measurement
1007: 
1008: ### 10.1 Per-session signals (computed by the pipeline after each episode)
1009: 
1010: | Metric | Definition | Target direction |
1011: |---|---|---|
1012: | **Rediscovery rate** | Share of extracted candidates that `support` an existing pushable claim which was *not* delivered in that session | ↓ |
1013: | **Repeated dead-end rate** | Sessions in which the agent attempted an approach matching a `verified` `ruled-out` claim | ↓ |
1014: | **Push precision** | Delivered claims that the agent referenced or acted on ÷ delivered claims | ↑ |
1015: | **Tokens pushed per session** | From the delivery ledger | Within budget |
1016: | **Sidecar tokens per session** | By stage | ↓ over time |
1017: | **Main-agent memory tokens** | Tokens the working agent spent writing memory artefacts | → 0 |
1018: | **Suppressed supports** | Candidates that would have supported a claim but were rejected under P13 because the session had been exposed to it | Monitored. A sudden rise signals a circularity leak or over-strict rules. |
1019: | **Interactive call rate** | LLM brief fallbacks, tier-2 checks and pull-tool syntheses per session, with their tokens | Within caps (§4.4.1) |
1020: | **Coverage** | §9.1 | ↑ |
1021: 
1022: ### 10.2 Offline tuning (replay)
1023: 
1024: Recorded episodes serve as a fixed benchmark for the **delivery policy** (trigger rules, budgets, ranking):
1025: 
1026: - For each episode, simulate delivery using only the episode *prefix* up to each step (prefix-only observability).
1027: - Label relevance from the *suffix*: did the session later touch the claim's anchors, hit its signature, or re-derive it?
1028: - A candidate policy replaces the current one only if it scores higher on the fixed set (in-sample no-regret selection, as in Dream-RSI).
1029: - Labels are proxies (delivering a claim would have changed the trajectory). Use replay for tuning and online metrics for acceptance.
1030: 
1031: ### 10.3 Acceptance benchmarks (for the build phases)
1032: 
1033: | ID | Benchmark |
1034: |---|---|
1035: | B1 | **pr-225 facts benchmark.** Build the claim store from events up to commit `69d9c813`. Give a fresh agent pr-225's original request plus memory delivery, and have it produce the equivalent of "Framework Facts Workers Need". Compare against the PA's hand-written section for correctness, completeness, tokens and tool calls. Baseline: the same task with today's PA memory. |
1036: | B2 | **Question bank.** ≥ 50 questions drawn from session logs and ADRs ("what's been ruled out for…", "why is X…", "what does error Y mean…"), answered with `memory.ask` vs. baseline. |
1037: | B3 | **Task replays.** 3–5 historical tasks re-run from their starting commits in worktrees (no hardware-in-the-loop), with and without memory. Measure turns, tokens and repeats of known dead-ends. |
1038: | B4 | **Cost.** Sidecar tokens (by stage, model tier and token type) vs. PA memory work for a comparable period. The PA side is broken down by activity: boot reads (frontier, input); session-log distillation (frontier, output); worker completion reports (worker model, output); "Framework Facts" sections (frontier, output); index graduation (frontier, output); Chief Architect programme logs (frontier, output). Priced per tier, not just summed. |
1039: | B5 | **Extraction precision.** A labelled sample of ≥ 20 episodes (OTA and BLE history). A human marks each extracted claim as correct / wrong / not durable, and lists durable knowledge the extractor missed. Reports precision and recall per claim type. |
1040: 
1041: **Gates.**
1042: 
1043: - **P1 exit** requires B5 precision ≥ 0.8 for claims that would be pushed (status `verified` or higher), plus B1 at parity with the PA's hand-written section on correctness and completeness.
1044: - **If B5 falls short**, the fallback is not to abandon the design:
1045:   1. Raise the triage threshold.
1046:   2. Restrict push to `merged` and `confirmed` claims.
1047:   3. Switch the `solo` profile to review-all.
1048:   4. Iterate on extraction. Because knowledge is event-sourced, re-projection applies the improved extractor to all history.
1049: 
1050:   The episode search (P0.5) keeps the system useful in the meantime.
1051:

1074: ## 11. Security and governance
1075: 
1076: ### 11.1 Privacy
1077: 
1078: - Raw transcripts and episodes stay on the developer's machine. Only claims, views and human review events go into the repository.
1079: - Claims must not quote conversation verbatim beyond short error strings. Extraction instructions and a post-extraction check enforce this.
1080: 
1081: ### 11.2 Poisoning and untrusted input
1082: 
1083: - Candidates derived from external content (web pages, third-party issues, fetched docs, dependency READMEs) carry `provenance: external`, max status `observed`, and are never pushed without human confirmation.
1084: - Claims whose statements instruct actions on credentials, deployment, network endpoints, signing keys or security settings are always `needs-review`, whatever their evidence.
1085: - Status can't be raised by retrieval or use (§5.3.2), which prevents self-reinforcement loops.
1086: 
1087: ### 11.3 Secrets
1088: 
1089: - Scrubbing at compaction (§5.1), plus a second secret scan on claim files before publish. Any hit blocks publish for that claim.
1090: 
1091: ### 11.4 Integrity
1092: 
1093: - A lint gate runs in CI on `.memory/`:
1094:   - schema validation;
1095:   - views match regeneration (no hand edits);
1096:   - every claim has ≥ 1 evidence entry;
1097:   - every anchor resolves or is flagged;
1098:   - no secrets.
1099: - The memory PR is the only write path to shared memory.

696: ### 12.3 Tick
697: 
698: `repo-memory tick` is a subcommand of the `repo-memory` Go binary (§18). It is not a daemon: each run does its work and exits. The order of work, the job table and the budgets are defined in §4.3.
699: 
700: - **Idle cost.** A tick with nothing to do makes no LLM calls and finishes in well under a second (program start-up plus a few file and hash checks).
701: - **Git events** are detected by comparing HEAD, `dependencies.lock` and the sdkconfig hashes with the previous tick. No git hooks are installed.
702: - **Housekeeping runs** are child processes started with `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING=1`, the working directory `<data-dir>/runs/<repo-id>/`, the configured model and `--print-timeout`. The tick waits for them within its budget; a run still going when the budget ends keeps the tick alive until its timeout, and the next tick skips (`tick.lock`).
703: - **Reports** are started with `agentapi new-conversation --title="[repo-memory] …"` and polled on later ticks, as in the bug-fixer tick dispatcher.
704: - **Publishing** runs git in the dedicated worktree (`<data-dir>/<repo-id>/worktree/`, branch `memory/pending`), never in the user's checkout.
705: 
706: **`repo-memory run`** is kept as an alias for `tick`, for manual use.

915: ### 7.8 Performance
916: 
917: Antigravity hooks run synchronously and block the agent loop, and `PreInvocation` runs before *every* model call. Latency therefore adds up: at 100 ms per call, a session with 300 model calls gains 30 s.
918: 
919: - **Delivery hook fast path.** Check the conversation's `alerts/` directory and read the transcript from the last cursor (tail only). If nothing new matches, exit. Target: p95 ≤ 60 ms, p50 ≤ 30 ms.
920: - **Delivery hook with injection.** Local SQLite read-only queries plus formatting. Target: p95 ≤ 150 ms.
921: - **Implementation.** Hooks run the compiled Go binary (§18), so start-up costs milliseconds. E5 confirms the fast-path budget on macOS and Windows.
922: - **Measurement.** Cumulative hook time per session is recorded (§10.4) and reported against a session budget (default ≤ 2% of wall-clock time).
923: - **Failure behaviour.** No LLM calls and no network in hooks. If the index is missing or locked, the hook exits with an empty injection. Memory must never block or break work.

938: ## 8. Validity and re-checking
939: 
940: Re-checks are triggered by dependency changes, never by time or disuse.
941: 
942: | Change detected | Claims affected | Action |
943: |---|---|---|
944: | Merge to main changes a file | Claims anchored to changed symbols or windows (fingerprint mismatch) | Set `suspect`; queue a behavioural verify; on pass, clear and restamp `verified_at`; on fail, send to Reconcile with the diff as evidence |
945: | Symbol or file deleted or renamed | Claims anchored to it | Attempt re-anchor (rename detection); else `needs-review` |
946: | `dependencies.lock` / `platformio.ini` / SDK version change | Claims whose `conditions` reference the changed item | Set `conditions-changed`; `ruled-out` claims are delivered as "may work now" |
947: | sdkconfig value change | Claims anchored to that config key | Set `suspect`; verify |
948: | Revert on main | Claims with the reverted commit as evidence | Re-evaluate |
949: | A closure condition fires: issue closed, branch merged, work order complete, or a later episode shows the success outcome | `open-issue` claims whose `closes_when` lists it (§5.3.1) | Set `resolved`, with the closing event as evidence. If a fixing episode exists, its own extraction may yield a `failure-signature` or `decision`. |
950: | Human correction | The named claim | Apply as a `confirmed` or `refuted` event |
951: 
952: **Evaluating closure conditions.** Branches and PA work orders are checked every tick (local git and PA ledger reads). Outcome conditions are checked as each new episode is processed. Issue state needs the network, so it is checked at most daily through the git host's CLI.
953: 
954: **Explicitly out of scope:** decay by age, decay by retrieval frequency, and confidence scores that change with use. A claim about a subsystem nobody has touched in a year is as valid as the day it was verified, because nothing it depends on has changed. `open-issue` claims are no exception: they close on events, not with age.

958: ## 9. Coverage and elicitation
959: 
960: ### 9.1 Coverage model
961: 
962: For each subsystem, the pipeline computes a coverage record:
963: 
964: | Dimension | Measure |
965: |---|---|
966: | Rationale | Number of `decision` claims vs. key design points (public interfaces, major files) |
967: | Invariants | Number of `invariant` claims and the share enforced by a test or gate |
968: | Verification | Presence of at least one `procedure` for testing or verifying the subsystem |
969: | Failure knowledge | `failure-signature` and `ruled-out` counts relative to churn and incident history |
970: | Freshness | Share of claims that are `suspect` or `conditions-changed`, and `open-issue` claims with `closes_when: unknown` |
971: | Referenced gaps | `gaps` reported by extraction (§6.5) for the subsystem and not yet covered by a claim, counted by how many episodes mention each |
972: 
973: **Gap score** = churn (commits in last 90 days) × complexity × (1 − coverage). Frequently referenced gaps are also candidates for elicitation questions (§9.2).
974: 
975: ### 9.2 Elicitation
976: 
977: - Weekly (configurable), the tick picks **1–3 targeted questions** for the highest gap scores. For example: "Why does DataManager use FetchContext deadlines rather than per-source timeouts?"
978: - Questions go into the weekly **review report**, an IDE-visible conversation (§4.4), never into a working session.
979: - The human answers in that conversation. The sweep captures the conversation, and the human's messages become `human_answers` events, which become `confirmed` claims. The report's own text is never treated as evidence.
980: - The questions are also written to a `QUESTIONS.md` view, so they can be answered later or by someone else.
981: 
982: #### 9.2.1 Reading replies from report conversations
983: 
984: Report conversations mix three kinds of text: the automated kickoff prompt, the report agent's generated text (derived from memory), and the human's replies. Only the last is evidence. The mechanism must not depend on an LLM guessing who said what:
985: 
986: 1. **Record what was asked.** When the tick starts a report, the job table records the conversation ID, the kickoff prompt's hash, and the question IDs and claim IDs presented (e.g. `Q-017`, `clm-…`).
987: 2. **Classify authors structurally.** Author classification (§5.1) uses the harness's own message roles, excluding the kickoff prompt. The report agent's text counts as an exposure to every claim it presented, so nothing it says can support those claims (P13).
988: 3. **Parse explicit commands mechanically, without an LLM,** from human-authored steps: `approve clm-…`, `reject clm-…`, `approve all <subsystem>`, and `Q-017: <answer>`. These become review events and `human_answers` events directly.
989: 4. **Interpret free-text replies conservatively.** A small model maps each reply to the question or claim IDs it addresses. The human's verbatim text is stored as the evidence.
990:    - A resulting claim is `confirmed` only if the reconciler finds the human's text states the fact explicitly.
991:    - Otherwise it is `needs-review`. The next report quotes the interpretation back for confirmation: "I understood X from your answer to Q-017. Correct?"
992: 5. **Give the report agent no memory-write tools.** It is instructed to present questions verbatim and never answer on the human's behalf. Anything it types is excluded structurally in any case.
993: 
994: ### 9.3 Inferred backfill
995: 
996: For subsystems with no rationale coverage, a one-off pass infers `decision` claims from code, commit messages and PR descriptions. These claims have status `hypothesis` and are tagged `inferred`. They're shown in views as "inferred, unconfirmed" and are never pushed until a human confirms them.
997: 
998: ### 9.4 Invariant enforcement
999: 
1000: Each `invariant` claim may carry `enforced_by: <test|lint|gate path>`. Unenforced invariants in high-churn subsystems are listed as **proposed work** in the weekly review report, for example "turn this invariant into a CI check". The memory system never changes code itself (§4.4). The human, a PA project or the bug-fixer loop picks up the work in an IDE session. Enforced invariants are re-checked by CI, not only by the pipeline.
1001: 
1002: Other proposals raised the same way include human-facing docs that contradict verified claims, and stale `framework-expert` skill sections.

1074: ## 11. Security and governance
1075: 
1076: ### 11.1 Privacy
1077: 
1078: - Raw transcripts and episodes stay on the developer's machine. Only claims, views and human review events go into the repository.
1079: - Claims must not quote conversation verbatim beyond short error strings. Extraction instructions and a post-extraction check enforce this.
1080: 
1081: ### 11.2 Poisoning and untrusted input
1082: 
1083: - Candidates derived from external content (web pages, third-party issues, fetched docs, dependency READMEs) carry `provenance: external`, max status `observed`, and are never pushed without human confirmation.
1084: - Claims whose statements instruct actions on credentials, deployment, network endpoints, signing keys or security settings are always `needs-review`, whatever their evidence.
1085: - Status can't be raised by retrieval or use (§5.3.2), which prevents self-reinforcement loops.
1086: 
1087: ### 11.3 Secrets
1088: 
1089: - Scrubbing at compaction (§5.1), plus a second secret scan on claim files before publish. Any hit blocks publish for that claim.
1090: 
1091: ### 11.4 Integrity
1092: 
1093: - A lint gate runs in CI on `.memory/`:
1094:   - schema validation;
1095:   - views match regeneration (no hand edits);
1096:   - every claim has ≥ 1 evidence entry;
1097:   - every anchor resolves or is flagged;
1098:   - no secrets.
1099: - The memory PR is the only write path to shared memory.

1235: ### 12.3 Tick
1236: 
1237: `repo-memory tick` is a subcommand of the `repo-memory` Go binary (§18). It is not a daemon: each run does its work and exits. The order of work, the job table and the budgets are defined in §4.3.
1238: 
1239: - **Idle cost.** A tick with nothing to do makes no LLM calls and finishes in well under a second (program start-up plus a few file and hash checks).
1240: - **Git events** are detected by comparing HEAD, `dependencies.lock` and the sdkconfig hashes with the previous tick. No git hooks are installed.
1241: - **Housekeeping runs** are child processes started with `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING=1`, the working directory `<data-dir>/runs/<repo-id>/`, the configured model and `--print-timeout`. The tick waits for them within its budget; a run still going when the budget ends keeps the tick alive until its timeout, and the next tick skips (`tick.lock`).
1242: - **Reports** are started with `agentapi new-conversation --title="[repo-memory] …"` and polled on later ticks, as in the bug-fixer tick dispatcher.
1243: - **Publishing** runs git in the dedicated worktree (`<data-dir>/<repo-id>/worktree/`, branch `memory/pending`), never in the user's checkout.
1244: 
1245: **`repo-memory run`** is kept as an alias for `tick`, for manual use.

991: ### 18.5 Hooks in Go
992: 
993: - **Invocation.** `hooks.json` entries call `<absolute path>/repo-memory hook antigravity <Event>`, written by `install`, so they work under `sh -c` and `cmd /c` without `PATH`.
994: - **Fast path.** The hook reads a per-conversation cursor (a byte offset into the transcript), reads only new bytes, checks `alerts/`, and opens SQLite read-only only when there is something to look up.
995: - **Budget.** p95 ≤ 60 ms on the fast path (§7.8), confirmed by E5 on macOS and Windows.
996: - **Failure behaviour.** On any error, the hook returns the harness's no-op output and logs the error. It never blocks the agent.
997: 
998: ### 18.6 Portability rules for Release 1
999: 
1000: Release 1 follows these rules so that Release 2 is an adapter, not a rewrite:
1001: 
1002: 1. **Core never sees native field names.** Everything harness-specific enters through the normalised types in `internal/harness` (`Event`, `Injection`, `Step`).
1003: 2. **Delivery decides by capability flags,** never by harness name (§18.3).
1004: 3. **Stage prompts and JSON schemas are executor-neutral files.** Executors only transport them.
1005: 4. **Stores, config and guards are harness-neutral:** the episode format, claim store, views, data directory, config keys (`housekeeping.executor`, `reports.surface`, `tick.trigger`) and the `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING` guard.
1006: 5. **Map and rule generation takes a target list.** Release 1 emits the Antigravity include and rules only, but the generator is written per target.
1007: 6. **Core tests run against the `fake` adapter,** so core can't silently depend on Antigravity behaviour.
1008: 7. **The adapter contract suite is reusable.** It is fixture in → expected normalised events and steps out, written in P2 for Antigravity and reused unchanged for Claude Code in R2.1.
1009: 8. **Episodes record `harness` and `harness_version`** from day one.
1010: 9. **Report content is generated by core** (Markdown plus question and claim IDs). The reporter only delivers it.
1011: 10. **Tick triggers are external.** The tick never assumes which harness or scheduler started it.
1012: 11. **Claude Code history is preserved from P0 (recommended).** The sweep copies Claude Code transcripts into `raw/claude-code/`, private and unparsed, with the same permissions as the originals. R2.1 compacts and scrubs them. This costs a few lines in the sweep and prevents the 30-day retention from erasing history before Release 2. Drop it for a strict Antigravity-only Release 1.

# repo-memory Programme

> **Programme:** Build `repo-memory`, a repository-level memory system for coding agents.
> **Specification:** [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) (v0.6, 2026-09-30)
> **Status:** Planning
> **Base branch:** `main`

## Programme Summary

Build a Go binary (`repo-memory`) that captures agent sessions, distils them into typed, evidence-backed claims, and delivers relevant knowledge back to working agents at the moment of need. Release 1 targets Antigravity; Release 2 adds Claude Code as an adapter (§15).

The system has two invocation paths (event hooks and a scheduled tick), a six-stage pipeline (Capture → Compact → Triage → Extract → Reconcile → Verify → Publish), and a delivery layer that pushes knowledge at task start, file touch, error, risky action and déjà-vu. Pull tools provide on-demand access. All data lives in files and SQLite; no daemon, no server, no cloud.

## Architecture Domains

| Domain | SPEC Sections | Key Components |
|---|---|---|
| **Core Infrastructure** | §18.1–18.6 | Go binary skeleton, CLI subcommands, config, data-dir layout, harness interfaces, capability types, package-boundary enforcement |
| **Harness: Antigravity** | §12.1 | Transcript parser, hook codec, `agy` executor, `agentapi` reporter, install templates |
| **Harness: Fake** | §18.2 | Test adapter driving the core test suite |
| **Capture** | §4.1–4.3, §6.2 | `Stop` hook, spool, transcript copy, sweep, idle promotion |
| **Compaction** | §5.1, §6.3 | Deterministic compaction, author classification, exposure markers, scrubber |
| **Episode Store** | §5.1, §5.6 | Private JSONL+zstd episodes, `episodes/` layout |
| **Job Table** | §4.3 | SQLite job table, spool ingestion, tick lock, leases, back-pressure |
| **Tick** | §4.3, §12.3 | Spool ingest → job table → sweep → jobs → calendar; tick.lock |
| **Entity Extraction** | §5.2 | Code-only (no LLM) entity extractor: files, symbols, configs, topics, tools, errors, externals; extractor rules |
| **Pipeline Stages 2–6** | §6.4–6.8 | Triage, Extract, Reconcile, Verify, Publish (including LLM housekeeping via `agy -p`) |
| **Claim Store** | §5.3, §5.6 | Claim file schema, month-sharded `.memory/claims/`, relations |
| **Views** | §5.5 | MAP.md, claim indexes, subsystem pages, SIGNATURES.md, DECISIONS.md |
| **Index** | §5.6, §18.4 | SQLite rebuildable index in `.memory/.cache/index.sqlite` |
| **Delivery** | §7 | Task brief, touch, error, risky action, déjà-vu tiers 0–2, budgets, ledger |
| **Pull Tools (MCP)** | §7.7, §18.1 | `memory.ask`, `memory.why`, `memory.history`, `memory.brief`, `memory.note`, `memory.stats` |
| **Validity & Re-checking** | §8 | Fingerprint change → suspect, conditions-changed, closure condition evaluation |
| **Coverage & Elicitation** | §9 | Coverage model, gap scores, elicitation questions, review reports, inferred backfill |
| **Measurement** | §10 | Per-session signals, offline replay tuning, acceptance benchmarks B1–B5, observability |
| **Security** | §11 | Scrubbing, provenance tagging, lint gate |
| **Publishing** | §6.8 | Two-lane publish, memory PR, review profiles, git worktree |
| **PA Integration** | §13 | Episode summaries, generated task briefs in WORKORDERs |
| **Backfill** | §14 | PA file import, transcript backfill |

## PR Sequence (linear dependency chain)

See [PROGRAM-PLAN.md](PROGRAM-PLAN.md) for the full dependency graph, scope per PR, and exit criteria.

| # | PR | SPEC Phase | Status | Depends On |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pr-01-go-skeleton` | P0 (partial) | ☐ Planned | — |
| 2 | `pr-02-capture` | P0 | ☐ Planned | PR-01 |
| 3 | `pr-03-episode-search` | P0.5 | ☐ Planned | PR-02 |
| 4 | `pr-04-entities-claims` | P1 (partial) | ☐ Planned | PR-03 |
| 5 | `pr-05-pipeline` | P1 | ☐ Planned | PR-04 |
| 6 | `pr-06-publish-review` | P1 (partial) | ☐ Planned | PR-05 |
| 7 | `pr-07-delivery` | P2 | ☐ Planned | PR-06 |
| 8 | `pr-08-learning-loop` | P3 | ☐ Planned | PR-07 |
| 9 | `pr-09-pa-integration` | P4 | ☐ Planned | PR-08 |
| 10 | `pr-10-backfill` | P5 | ☐ Planned | PR-09 |
| 11 | `pr-11-experiments` | P0 (E1–E11) | ☐ Planned | PR-02 |

## Human Approval

- [ ] Programme plan reviewed and approved
- [ ] PR sequence confirmed

## Session Log

### 2026-10-01 — Programme planning (session 1)

- Read SPEC.md v0.6 (1615 lines) cover to cover.
- Identified 11 PRs across Release 1's 6 build phases (P0–P5).
- The SPEC's phases are large: P0 alone covers the Go skeleton, all four hooks, the tick sidecar, the job table, compaction, scrubbing, episodes, metrics, and 11 experiments. This is decomposed across PR-01 (skeleton), PR-02 (capture), and PR-11 (experiments).
- P1 is the heaviest phase: entity extraction, all 6 pipeline stages, claims, views, the lint gate, two-lane publish, review reports, and OTA/BLE import. Decomposed across PR-04, PR-05, and PR-06.
- Release 2 (Claude Code) is intentionally excluded from this plan per the SPEC: it starts after P2 and is an adapter, not a rewrite, thanks to §18.6 portability rules.
- Created the programme workspace, provisioned the operating-model rule, initialized memory.

# repo-memory — Programme Plan

> **Programme:** repo-memory
> **Specification:** [SPEC.md](../../../SPEC.md) v0.6
> **Release:** 1 (Antigravity)
> **Created:** 2026-10-01
> **Total PRs:** 11
> **Dependency model:** Linear chain (PR-01 → PR-10), with PR-11 branching off PR-02

---

## Dependency Graph

```
PR-01  Go Skeleton & Interfaces
  │
  ▼
PR-02  Capture (Stop hook, tick, sweep, compaction, episodes)
  │
  ├──────────────────────────────┐
  ▼                              ▼
PR-03  Episode Search (FTS)    PR-11  P0 Experiments (E1–E11)
  │
  ▼
PR-04  Entities, Claims & Index (data model)
  │
  ▼
PR-05  Pipeline Stages 2–6 (triage → extract → reconcile → verify)
  │
  ▼
PR-06  Publish, Views & Review (two-lane publish, lint gate, reports)
  │
  ▼
PR-07  Delivery (hooks, pull tools, budgets, degraded modes)
  │
  ▼
PR-08  Learning Loop (déjà-vu tier 2, coverage, elicitation, metrics, replay)
  │
  ▼
PR-09  PA Integration (episode summaries, generated briefs, retire indexes)
  │
  ▼
PR-10  Full Backfill (all remaining history, inferred rationale, re-projection)
```

---

## PR-01: Go Skeleton & Interfaces

**SPEC Sections:** §18.1–18.6, §4.5, §5.6 (layout only)

**Objective:** Establish the Go module, binary entry point, subcommand wiring, package layout with the enforced core/adapter boundary, the harness interface types, and the `fake` test adapter. This PR produces a binary that compiles and responds to `hook`, `tick`, `mcp`, `install`, `status`, `doctor` — all returning stubs or no-ops.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-go-module` | `go mod init`, `cmd/repo-memory/main.go`, subcommand wiring (cobra or manual), `Makefile`/`taskfile` for cross-compile (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). Verify `darwin/arm64`, `linux/amd64`, `windows/amd64` cross-compile. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-package-layout` | Create all `internal/core/*` and `internal/harness/*` packages as empty stubs with package docs. Write the import-graph boundary test: `internal/core` must not import any concrete adapter. | standard |
| 3 | `wo3-harness-interfaces` | Define `Harness`, `Capabilities`, `TranscriptSource`, `HookCodec`, `Reporter`, `Housekeeper` interfaces in `internal/harness/`. Define normalised types: `Event`, `Injection`, `Step`. Define `Stage` enum for pipeline stages. | standard |
| 4 | `wo4-fake-adapter` | Implement `internal/harness/fake/` — a test adapter that satisfies all interfaces with in-memory state. Write the core test suite shell that runs against `fake`. | standard |
| 5 | `wo5-config-datadir` | `internal/core/config/`: load `config.yaml` (subsystems, budgets, trigger settings). `internal/core/config/datadir.go`: platform-appropriate data directory (`~/Library/Application Support/repo-memory` on macOS, etc.). Create storage layout dirs on first run. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-subcommand-stubs` | Wire `hook`, `tick`, `mcp`, `install`, `search`, `report`, `status`, `reindex`, `doctor` as subcommands. Each prints a stub message. `install --harness antigravity` generates plugin files from `packaging/antigravity/` templates (with absolute binary path). | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- `go build ./cmd/repo-memory` succeeds for all 5 targets
- `repo-memory status` runs and exits 0
- `repo-memory install --harness antigravity` generates correct `hooks.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `sidecar.json`
- Import-graph boundary test passes
- Core tests run against the `fake` adapter

---

## PR-02: Capture

**SPEC Sections:** §4.1–4.3, §5.1, §6.2–6.3, §11.3, §10.4 (metrics skeleton)

**Objective:** Every Antigravity session produces a compacted, scrubbed episode within minutes of going idle. The tick sidecar processes the spool and manages the job table. Claude Code transcripts are sweep-copied to `raw/` for future R2 processing.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-spool-format` | Define spool entry schema. Implement `spool/` writer: atomic write-then-rename. Implement spool reader for the tick. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-stop-hook` | `internal/harness/antigravity/hooks.go`: handle `Stop` event. Write spool entry, copy transcript to `queue/`. Budget: ≤ 200 ms. `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING` environment guard. | standard |
| 3 | `wo3-transcript-parser` | `internal/harness/antigravity/transcript.go`: parse Antigravity `transcript.jsonl` into `[]episode.Step`. Handle `CHECKPOINT` steps, step gaps, `source`/`type` classification. Scrub fixture transcripts for test data. | architect |
| 4 | `wo4-compaction` | `internal/core/pipeline/compact/`: deterministic compaction per §5.1 rules. Author classification (`human` vs `automation`). Exposure markers. Secret scrubber (pattern + entropy). Output: episode JSONL. Target: ≥ 4× reduction. | architect |
| 5 | `wo5-episode-store` | `internal/core/episode/store.go`: write episodes as `<data-dir>/<repo-id>/episodes/<yyyy>/<session-id>.jsonl.zst`. Episode header schema. Gap recording. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-job-table` | `internal/core/jobs/`: SQLite job table (§4.3). Schema: `id`, `kind`, `priority`, `idempotency_key`, `state`, `lease_expires`, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `cost`. State machine: `queued` → `running` → `done` / `failed` → `dead`. Lease recovery. | standard |
| 7 | `wo7-tick-core` | `internal/core/tick/`: the tick loop per §4.3. `tick.lock` (flock). Spool ingestion → job creation. Lease reclaim. Sweep transcripts (Antigravity app, CLI, and Claude Code raw copy). Idle promotion (15 min). Budget enforcement. | architect |
| 8 | `wo8-antigravity-sidecar` | `packaging/antigravity/sidecars/tick/sidecar.json`: `builtin: schedule`, `* * * * *`. Update `install` to generate it. | mechanical |
| 9 | `wo9-metrics-skeleton` | `internal/core/metrics/`: JSONL metrics writer. Record: capture health (sessions seen, captured, skipped, missed), hook execution time, tick duration, budget exhaustion. | standard |
| 10 | `wo10-claude-raw-copy` | Sweep extension: copy Claude Code transcripts from `~/.claude/projects/` to `<data-dir>/<repo-id>/raw/claude-code/`. No parsing. Respects the same permissions. | mechanical |

### Exit Criteria
- Every new Antigravity session produces an episode within minutes of going idle
- Sessions captured before their transcripts disappear
- Share caught only by sweep: measured
- Compaction ratio ≥ 4× measured
- Zero secrets in a scan of 50 episodes
- Core tests pass on the `fake` adapter
- `internal/core` imports no concrete adapter

---

## PR-03: Episode Search

**SPEC Sections:** §15.1 P0.5

**Objective:** Make captured history searchable before the knowledge pipeline exists. Import PA files as searchable episodes.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-fts-index` | SQLite FTS5 index over episodes. Columns: `episode_id`, `session_id`, `content` (compacted text), `files_touched`, `outcomes`, `date`. Populate from the episode store. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-search-cli` | `repo-memory search <query>`: full-text search over episodes. Output: episode ID, date, branch, snippet, files. Rank by BM25. | standard |
| 3 | `wo3-pa-import` | Import PA `PROJECT.md`, `WORKORDER.md`, `context_bridge.md` files as episodes with `harness: "import"`. Date from file or git history. One episode per file. | standard |
| 4 | `wo4-ask-fallback` | `memory.ask` MCP tool: when no claims exist yet, fall back to FTS over episodes. Mark results as "unverified (episode search)". | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- Can find what was tried, and when, across all captured and imported history
- PA workspace files searchable
- `memory.ask` returns relevant episodes with "unverified" marking

---

## PR-04: Entities, Claims & Index

**SPEC Sections:** §5.2, §5.3, §5.4, §5.5 (index only), §5.6 (claims/), §18.4

**Objective:** Build the data model layer: entity extraction from the repository (no LLM), the claim file schema and store, and the rebuildable SQLite index. This is the foundation the pipeline writes into and delivery reads from.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-entity-types` | `internal/core/entities/`: entity types (`subsystem`, `file`, `symbol`, `config`, `env`, `topic`, `tool`, `error`, `external`). Entity relations (`contains`, `depends_on`, `implements`, `configures`). Entity registry in the index. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-entity-extractor` | No-LLM entity extractor: tree walk for files (`.gitignore`-aware), parse `sdkconfig`/Kconfig/`platformio.ini`/lockfiles for configs, brace-aware C/C++ symbol scanner (ctags fallback), extractor rules from `config.yaml` for topics/tools/errors. | architect |
| 3 | `wo3-claim-schema` | `internal/core/claims/`: claim file parser and writer. YAML frontmatter + Markdown body. All fields from §5.3: `id`, `type`, `title`, `relevant_when`, `apply`, `status`, `flags`, `anchors`, `conditions`, `evidence`, `relations`, `scope`, `verified_at`, `provenance`, `review`, `match` blocks, `closes_when`. ULID generation. | standard |
| 4 | `wo4-claim-store` | `.memory/claims/<yyyy-mm>/` layout. CRUD operations. Month-sharded writes. Relation index (inverse lookups). | standard |
| 5 | `wo5-sqlite-index` | `internal/core/index/`: rebuildable SQLite index in `.memory/.cache/index.sqlite`. Tables: entities, claims, anchors, relations, conditions. Built from claim files + entity registry. `repo-memory reindex` command. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-subsystem-config` | `.memory/config.yaml` subsystem configuration. Glob matching for file→subsystem assignment. Unassigned file detection. Subsystem bootstrap proposal (one-off LLM pass, deferred to PR-05). | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- Entity extractor produces correct entities from the esp32-app-foundation structure (or test fixture)
- Claim files round-trip (write → read → write produces identical output)
- Index is rebuildable from claim files and entities
- `repo-memory reindex` works
- All entity kinds from §5.2 are extractable

---

## PR-05: Pipeline Stages 2–6

**SPEC Sections:** §6.4–6.7, §6.9

**Objective:** The knowledge pipeline: triage, extract, reconcile, verify. Each stage is a pure function dispatched to `agy -p`. The pipeline turns episodes into claims in the store.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-agy-executor` | `internal/harness/antigravity/executor.go`: `Housekeeper` implementation. Invoke `agy -p` with `--model`, `--json-schema`, `--output-format json`, `--input-format stream-json`, `--print-timeout`. Parse JSON response and `usage`. Set `REPO_MEMORY_HOUSEKEEPING=1`. Working dir: `<data-dir>/runs/<repo-id>/`. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-triage` | `internal/core/pipeline/triage/`: rule-based triage (§6.4). Keep/skip rules. Salience window selection. Synopsis generation. Small-model fallback for ambiguous episodes. Prompt and JSON schema in `prompts/triage/`. | architect |
| 3 | `wo3-extract` | `internal/core/pipeline/extract/`: extraction stage (§6.5). Pack episodes to 60k input cap. 20-candidate-per-episode limit. Prompt enforces all 11 extraction rules. Output: candidate claims with anchors, evidence, `gaps`. Evidence independence (P13). `prompts/extract/`. | architect |
| 4 | `wo4-reconcile` | `internal/core/pipeline/reconcile/`: reconciliation (§6.6). Look up existing claims by anchor (bounded to 30). Stronger model. 7 operations: create, support, refine, contradict, supersede, promote, discard. P13 enforcement. Single-writer constraint. `prompts/reconcile/`. | architect |
| 5 | `wo5-verify` | `internal/core/pipeline/verify/`: verification (§6.7). Anchor resolution and fingerprinting. Behavioural check (small model on code snippets). Branch scoping rules. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-subsystem-bootstrap` | One-off LLM pass to propose subsystems and globs from directory structure and existing docs. Output: proposed `config.yaml` for human review. | standard |
| 7 | `wo7-pipeline-orchestration` | Wire stages 2–6 into the tick's job processing. Respect concurrency rules (extraction parallel; reconcile and publish single-writer). Idempotency keys per stage. Cost recording per stage. | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- **Gate: B5** precision ≥ 0.8 for pushable claims (verified or higher)
- **Gate: B1** at parity with the PA's hand-written facts section
- B2 shows improvement over baseline (episode search)
- Pipeline cost per episode and per stage measured
- Stages are idempotent (re-running produces identical results)

---

## PR-06: Publish, Views & Review

**SPEC Sections:** §5.5, §6.8, §9.2.1, §11.4

**Objective:** Two-lane publish (local immediate + shared memory PR), generated views, the lint gate, weekly review reports with reply parsing, and review profiles.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-local-publish` | `internal/core/pipeline/publish/local.go`: write new/changed claims to `<data-dir>/<repo-id>/pending/`. Index immediately. Mark as `unreviewed`. Security and external provenance gating. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-shared-publish` | `internal/core/pipeline/publish/shared.go`: batch pending ops into a memory PR on `memory/pending` branch. Git worktree operations (`<data-dir>/<repo-id>/worktree/`). PR description grouped by subsystem. Never commit to user's branch. | architect |
| 3 | `wo3-views` | `internal/core/views/`: generate MAP.md (≤ 2k tokens), claim indexes per subsystem (≤ 1.5k tokens), subsystem pages (≤ 5k tokens), SIGNATURES.md, DECISIONS.md. Budget enforcement with re-synthesis. Regenerate on claim/entity changes. | architect |
| 4 | `wo4-lint-gate` | CI lint gate for `.memory/`: schema validation, views match regeneration, every claim has ≥ 1 evidence, every anchor resolves or flagged, no secrets. `repo-memory lint` command. | standard |
| 5 | `wo5-review-profiles` | `config.yaml` → `review.profile`: `solo` (default) and `team` profiles per §6.8. Auto-merge rules per operation type. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-review-report` | Weekly review report via `agentapi new-conversation`. Reply parsing (§9.2.1): explicit command parsing, conservative free-text interpretation. Author classification. Human replies → `human_answers` events and review events. | architect |

### Exit Criteria
- Memory PR is generated with correct grouping and evidence links
- Views regenerate correctly and stay within budget
- Lint gate catches: missing evidence, hand-edited views, unresolved anchors, secrets
- Review report parses `approve clm-…` and `Q-017: <answer>` commands
- Review profiles apply correctly

---

## PR-07: Delivery

**SPEC Sections:** §7, §18.3 (capability-based policy), §18.5

**Objective:** The read side: hooks deliver knowledge at task start, file touch, error, risky action, and déjà-vu tier 0/1. Pull tools provide on-demand access. Performance within §7.8 budgets.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-delivery-engine` | `internal/core/delivery/`: normalised delivery engine. Capability-based policy (§18.3). Delivery ledger (per-session, per-claim). Token budgets (§7.1). Rendering: `apply` line + ID + currency stamp. Anchor-existence fast check. | architect |
| 2 | `wo2-preinvocation` | `PreInvocation` hook handler: fast path (p95 ≤ 60 ms). Check `alerts/`, read transcript tail from cursor. `invocationNum == 0`: task brief. Touch and error injection. Déjà-vu tier 1 on reasoning. Spool tier-2 requests. | architect |
| 3 | `wo3-pretooluse` | `PreToolUse` hook handler: risky-action gates (`gate-once`, `ask`, `next-invocation`). Déjà-vu tier 1 on concrete tool calls. Coexistence with existing gates. | standard |
| 4 | `wo4-posttooluse` | `PostToolUse` hook handler: detect git merge/checkout/pull/rebase/dependency update from transcript step at `stepIdx`. Spool re-check request. | mechanical |
| 5 | `wo5-map-include` | `AGENTS.md` include of `.memory/views/MAP.md`. Fallback: `PreInvocation` injection at `invocationNum == 0`. | mechanical |
| 6 | `wo6-pull-tools` | `internal/mcpserver/`: stdio MCP server. All six tools: `memory.ask`, `memory.why`, `memory.history`, `memory.brief`, `memory.note`, `memory.stats`. `ask` and `brief` may invoke synchronous housekeeping runs. Instrument all calls. | architect |
| 7 | `wo7-rules-generation` | Generate `rules/AGENTS.md` for the plugin: how to use memory tools, walk MAP → claim index, currency stamp semantics. Generate path-scoped rules (after E4 results). | standard |
| 8 | `wo8-degraded-modes` | Test and implement all 6 degraded modes from §7.9. Graceful fallback at each level. | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- B3 task replays run
- Per-session push within budget (20k tokens)
- Hook latency: fast path p95 ≤ 60 ms, injection p95 ≤ 150 ms (macOS and Windows)
- Degraded modes tested (no ticks, no housekeeping, no index, native floor, plugin off)
- Adapter contract suite green

---

## PR-08: Learning Loop

**SPEC Sections:** §7.6 (tier 2), §8, §9, §10.1–10.2

**Objective:** Déjà-vu tier 2 (semantic, via tick housekeeping run), validity re-checking, coverage and elicitation, per-session metrics, and offline replay tuning.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wo1-dejavu-tier2` | Tier-2 déjà-vu: tick batches pending semantic checks into one housekeeping run. Alert written to `alerts/`. Rate limiting (one in-flight, one per 5 model calls). Per-day caps. | standard |
| 2 | `wo2-recheck` | `internal/core/pipeline/verify/recheck.go`: re-check scheduler (§8). Fingerprint comparison, `suspect`/`conditions-changed` flagging. Closure condition evaluation (git + PA ledger + issue state daily). Rename detection for re-anchoring. | architect |
| 3 | `wo3-coverage` | `internal/core/metrics/coverage.go`: coverage model per subsystem (§9.1). Gap score computation. Gap aggregation from extraction. | standard |
| 4 | `wo4-elicitation` | Tick picks 1–3 targeted questions from highest gap scores. Written to the weekly review report and `QUESTIONS.md` view. Human answers → `confirmed` claims. | standard |
| 5 | `wo5-session-metrics` | Per-session signals (§10.1): rediscovery rate, repeated dead-end rate, push precision, tokens pushed, sidecar tokens, main-agent memory tokens, suppressed supports, interactive call rate. Computed after each episode. | standard |
| 6 | `wo6-replay-tuning` | Offline replay (§10.2): simulate delivery on episode prefixes. Label from suffix. Policy comparison. | architect |
| 7 | `wo7-report-cli` | `repo-memory report`: aggregate metrics from `metrics/*.jsonl`. Output: claim counts, delivery hit-rate, pipeline cost, coverage gaps. Also backs `memory.stats` detail. | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- Rediscovery and repeated dead-end rates reported weekly
- First policy update accepted by replay
- Coverage model produces meaningful gap scores
- Elicitation questions appear in review reports

---

## PR-09: PA Integration

**SPEC Sections:** §13

**Objective:** Replace hand-written PA memory with generated episode summaries and task briefs. Retire knowledge indexes.

| 3 | `wo3-retire-indexes` | PROJECT.md holds intent, plan, ledger, approvals only. Knowledge indexes replaced by generated views. Migration: existing index content → claims (import episodes). | standard |

### Exit Criteria
- Main-agent memory-writing tokens ≈ 0 for a full project cycle
- B4 shows lower total cost than PA hand-written memory

**SPEC Sections:** §14, §9.3

**Objective:** Import all remaining history. Inferred rationale pass. Re-projection tooling. Every subsystem has a page.

### Work Orders

### Exit Criteria
- Every subsystem has a page
- Coverage report published
- Historical defects end as `superseded` or `refuted`, not open

## PR-11: P0 Experiments

**SPEC Sections:** §12.1.1

**Objective:** Answer experiments E1–E11 before P2 builds on them. Can run in parallel with PR-03+.

### Work Orders

| # | WO | Scope | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | `wo2-e2-includes` | E2: Do `@[…](path)` includes in root `AGENTS.md` resolve and refresh? | interactive |

| 4 | `wo4-e4-rule-activation` | E4: Are Glob and Model Decision rule activations supported? | interactive |
| 5 | `wo5-e5-latency` | E5: Delivery hook latency of Go binary on macOS and Windows. | interactive |
| 6 | `wo6-e6-sidecar-behaviour` | E6: Sidecar ticking with CLI-only, sleep/wake, overlap handling. | interactive |
| 7 | `wo7-e7-isolation` | E7: Housekeeping run isolation (`--project`, `--continue`, history). | interactive |
| 8 | `wo8-e8-subagent-hooks` | E8: Do subagent conversations fire their own hooks? | interactive |
| 9 | `wo9-e9-deny-behaviour` | E9: How does `PreToolUse` `deny` + `reason` behave in practice? | interactive |
| 10 | `wo10-e10-overhead` | E10: Can ~17k-token overhead be reduced? Cache prefix behaviour. | interactive |
| 11 | `wo11-e11-quota` | E11: How do housekeeping runs count against quota? Rate limits. | interactive |

### Exit Criteria
- Each experiment has a documented answer with evidence
- Results feed into PR-07 delivery design decisions

---

## Risk Register

| Risk | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| B5 extraction precision < 0.8 at P1 exit | Defined fallback in SPEC §10.3: raise triage threshold, restrict push, review-all, iterate. Episode search keeps system useful. | PR-05 PA |
| Housekeeping overhead dominates small calls | E10 results feed into batching and caching strategy. Per-day caps. | PR-11, then PR-08 |
| Hook latency budget exceeded | Go binary solves interpreter start-up. E5 benchmarks before delivery is built. | PR-11, then PR-07 |
| Compaction ratio < 4× | Tuning rules. Tool traffic is 70–90% of transcripts, which is removed. | PR-02 PA |
| Sidecar doesn't tick in CLI-only mode | E6 answers this. OS scheduler fallback. | PR-11 |
| Claims at scale cause GitHub UI issues | Month sharding keeps < 1k per directory. Verified in §5.3. | PR-04 |

---

## Decision Log

| # | Decision | Date | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| PD1 | Decompose SPEC P0 across PR-01 (skeleton) and PR-02 (capture) | 2026-10-01 | P0 is too large for a single PR. Skeleton is independently testable. |
| PD2 | Decompose SPEC P1 across PR-04 (data model), PR-05 (pipeline), PR-06 (publish) | 2026-10-01 | P1 covers entities, 5 pipeline stages, views, publish, and review — too much for one PR. |

| PD4 | Release 2 (Claude Code) excluded from this plan | 2026-10-01 | Per SPEC §15.2: starts after P2 (PR-07). Portability rules in §18.6 ensure R2 is an adapter. |
| PD5 | All PRs in a linear chain (except PR-11) | 2026-10-01 | Each PR builds directly on the previous one's types and stores. Parallel PRs would cause constant merge conflicts in shared packages. |

# repo-memory — Programme Decomposition

> Chief Architect plan for implementing [SPEC.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/repo-memory-plugin/SPEC.md) v0.6

## Overview

The SPEC defines a repository-level memory system built as a single Go binary (`repo-memory`) with two invocation paths (hooks and a scheduled tick), a six-stage knowledge pipeline, and a delivery layer. Release 1 targets Antigravity; Release 2 adds Claude Code.

I've decomposed this into **11 PRs** across Release 1's 6 build phases (P0–P5), each with atomic work orders.

## Dependency Graph

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR01["PR-01: Go Skeleton & Interfaces\n§18 · 6 WOs"]
    PR02["PR-02: Capture\n§4, §5.1, §6.2–6.3 · 10 WOs"]
    PR03["PR-03: Episode Search\n§15.1 P0.5 · 4 WOs"]
    PR04["PR-04: Entities, Claims & Index\n§5.2–5.4 · 6 WOs"]
    PR05["PR-05: Pipeline Stages 2–6\n§6.4–6.9 · 7 WOs"]
    PR06["PR-06: Publish, Views & Review\n§5.5, §6.8, §9.2.1 · 6 WOs"]
    PR07["PR-07: Delivery\n§7, §18.3 · 8 WOs"]
    PR08["PR-08: Learning Loop\n§7.6, §8–10 · 7 WOs"]
    PR09["PR-09: PA Integration\n§13 · 3 WOs"]
    PR10["PR-10: Full Backfill\n§14, §9.3 · 5 WOs"]
    PR11["PR-11: P0 Experiments\n§12.1.1 · 11 WOs"]

    PR01 --> PR02
    PR02 --> PR03
    PR02 --> PR11
    PR03 --> PR04
    PR04 --> PR05
    PR05 --> PR06

    style PR08 fill:#f3e5f5
    style PR09 fill:#f3e5f5
    style PR10 fill:#f3e5f5
    style PR11 fill:#e1f5fe
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Colour key:** 🔵 P0 Capture · 🟢 P0.5 Search · 🟠 P1 Knowledge · 🔴 P2 Delivery · 🟣 P3–P5 Learning/Integration/Backfill

## PR Summary Table

| # | PR | Phase | WOs | Key Exit Gate | Est. Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Go Skeleton & Interfaces** | P0 | 6 | Binary compiles for all targets; boundary test passes | Medium |
| 2 | **Capture** | P0 | 10 | Every session → episode; compaction ≥ 4×; zero secrets | High |
| 3 | **Episode Search** | P0.5 | 4 | PA history searchable; `memory.ask` fallback works | Low |
| 4 | **Entities, Claims & Index** | P1 | 6 | Entity extractor, claim roundtrip, index rebuild | Medium |
| 5 | **Pipeline Stages 2–6** | P1 | 7 | **B5 precision ≥ 0.8; B1 parity with PA facts** | High |
| 6 | **Publish, Views & Review** | P1 | 6 | Memory PR, views, lint gate, review reports | High |
| 7 | **Delivery** | P2 | 8 | **B3 replays; hook latency ≤ 60ms; degraded modes** | High |
| 8 | **Learning Loop** | P3 | 7 | Metrics reported weekly; first replay policy update | Medium |
| 9 | **PA Integration** | P4 | 3 | Memory-writing tokens ≈ 0; B4 cost comparison | Low |
| 10 | **Full Backfill** | P5 | 5 | Every subsystem has a page; coverage published | Medium |
| 11 | **Experiments** | P0 | 11 | E1–E11 answered with evidence | Medium |

**Total: 73 Work Orders**

## Key Architectural Decisions

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| PD1 | Split SPEC P0 into PR-01 (skeleton) + PR-02 (capture) | P0 covers the Go skeleton, all hooks, tick, job table, compaction, scrubber, episodes, metrics — too large for one PR |
| PD2 | Split SPEC P1 into PR-04 (data model) + PR-05 (pipeline) + PR-06 (publish) | P1 covers entities, 5 LLM stages, views, publish, lint gate, review reports — three distinct concerns |
| PD3 | PR-11 (experiments) branches off PR-02 | Experiments need working hooks and sidecar; can run in parallel with PR-03+ |
| PD4 | Linear chain, not parallel PRs | Every PR builds on the previous one's types, stores, and interfaces — parallel work would mean constant merge conflicts in `internal/core` |
| PD5 | Release 2 excluded from this plan | Per SPEC §15.2, R2 starts after P2 and is an adapter not a rewrite |

## Risk Highlights

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **B5 precision < 0.8** (the P1 exit gate) | Blocks PR-06 → PR-07 | SPEC defines a 4-step fallback (§10.3); episode search keeps system useful |
| **Hook latency budget** (p95 ≤ 60ms) | Slows every agent session | Go binary eliminates interpreter start-up; E5 benchmarks before delivery is built |
| **Housekeeping overhead** (~17k tokens/call) | Cost scales with interactive calls | E10 answers overhead reduction; batching and caching strategies |
| **Compaction ratio < 4×** | Larger episodes → higher extraction cost | Tool traffic is 70–90% of transcripts — removing it should easily hit 4× |

## Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [PROGRAM.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/repo-memory-plugin/.agents/skills/principal-architect-workspace/programme-repo-memory/PROGRAM.md) | Programme overview, domain map, PR sequence, session log |
| [PROGRAM-PLAN.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/repo-memory-plugin/.agents/skills/principal-architect-workspace/programme-repo-memory/PROGRAM-PLAN.md) | Full plan: all 11 PRs with WO breakdowns, exit criteria, risk register |
| [MEMORY.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/repo-memory-plugin/.agents/skills/principal-architect-workspace/memory/MEMORY.md) | PA boot registry |
| [00-operating-model.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/repo-memory-plugin/.agents/rules/00-operating-model.md) | Governance rule for worker delegation |

## Next Steps

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Your approval is needed before execution begins.** Once you approve this programme plan, I will:
> 1. Start **PR-01: Go Skeleton & Interfaces** — creating the branch and spawning the Tier 2 PA to decompose it into detailed WORKORDERs and execute the 6 work orders.
> 2. Each subsequent PR starts when its predecessor is complete and merged.
> 3. PR-11 (Experiments) can start as soon as PR-02 is merged.

Do you want to:
- **Approve** the plan and start PR-01?
- **Modify** the PR decomposition (add, merge, split, or reorder PRs)?
- **Ask questions** about any specific PR, work order, or risk?

14: ## 1. Purpose
15: 
16: An agent starting work on a large, long-lived repository should behave as if it had been on the project from day one. It should know how each part of the system works and why. It should know what invariants must hold and what has already been tried and failed. It should know what a given error usually means and how to verify a change on real hardware.
17: 
18: This specification defines a memory system that provides that knowledge:
19: 
20: - **automatically**, without the working agent spending tokens to record it;
21: - **efficiently**, delivering only what the current task, file, error or action needs;
22: - **accurately**, keeping each fact tied to the code and evidence it depends on;
23: - **completely**, covering every part of the system, including stable parts nobody has touched for months.
24: 
25: ### 1.1 Goals
26: 
27: | # | Goal |
28: |---|---|
29: | G1 | The working agent writes no memory. All capture and distillation is done by a background sidecar. |
30: | G2 | Every subsystem in the repo has memory coverage, whether or not a conversation has discussed it. |
31: | G3 | Knowledge is delivered at the moment of need (task start, file touch, error, risky action), not only on request. |
32: | G4 | A fact stays valid until something it depends on changes. Age and lack of use never retire knowledge. |
33: | G5 | Trust is earned from outcomes (tests, builds, flash logs, merges, human confirmation), never from retrieval frequency or self-rated confidence. |
34: | G6 | Memory is rebuildable. Improving the pipeline and re-running it over the full history improves all past memory. |
35: | G7 | Knowledge that lives in git is human-readable, reviewable per fact, and merge-safe. |
36: | G8 | The system measures its own effectiveness using signals every session produces. |
37: | G9 | Existing artefacts (PA workspaces, ADRs, design specs, commit history) can be ingested without a special migration path. |
38: 
39: ### 1.2 Non-goals
40: 
41: - Generic chat or personal-assistant memory (user preferences across unrelated projects).
42: - Replacing git, the issue tracker or human-facing documentation. Memory can *feed* documentation (§7.3) but doesn't own it.
43: - A graph database, cloud vector store or any server infrastructure.
44: - Autonomous commits to the user's working branches.
45: - Storing what can be derived cheaply from the code at read time (structure, signatures, call graphs).

287:### 4.6 Repository enrolment and the kill switch
289:The plugin is installed globally, so its hooks fire in every workspace the harness opens, and `PreInvocation` fires on every model call. Memory must therefore act only on repositories the user has explicitly enrolled, and must cost almost nothing everywhere else.
295:3. registers the repository in `<data-dir>/registry.json`: repo ID (hash of the root commit), root path and known worktree paths;
298:**What enrolment controls:**
302:| Hooks | The first thing every hook does is map the workspace path to the registry (a small file, cached by modification time). If the workspace isn't enrolled, the hook returns the harness's no-op output at once: within 5 ms of process start. |
303:| Capture sweep | Copies only transcripts whose workspace matches an enrolled root or one of its worktrees. Sessions in other workspaces are never read or copied. |
304:| Tick | Processes enrolled repositories only. |
307:**Leaving.** `repo-memory leave` removes the registry entry. It doesn't touch `.memory/`, which is shared repository content. `--purge` also deletes that repository's private episodes and data directory.
309:**Kill switch.** One check comes before everything else in every hook and every tick: the environment variable `REPO_MEMORY_DISABLED=1`, or `enabled: false` in the machine configuration (`<data-dir>/config.yaml`). `repo-memory disable` and `repo-memory enable` set it, globally or with `--repo` for one repository. When disabled, hooks return no-op output and the tick exits. 13: ## Spawn Mechanics
14: 
15: Spawn workers using the **`invoke_subagent`** tool with `TypeName: "self"` — this inherits the full harness configuration including tools, skills, and system prompt, making it the correct type for capable execution workers.

27: ### `Workspace` Mode Decision

29: > [!CAUTION]
30: > **`"branch"` creates an isolated worktree at a path outside the user's permitted
31: > directory** (e.g. inside `~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/.../worktrees/`). The subagent
32: > will have **no permissions** for that path and will prompt the user for approval on
33: > every single file read or write. This defeats the purpose of autonomous execution.

3: This reference dictates how the `principal-architect` agent must manage stacked Pull Requests on GitHub. 5: ## 1. Branches & Base Resolution
6: 
7: ### 1.1 Branch Naming Conventions & The Immutable Head Rule
8: Because GitHub assigns PR IDs sequentially based on server activity, you cannot predict a PR ID at branch creation. Furthermore, **never rename the head branch of an open Pull Request.** GitHub hardcodes the `headRefName`; renaming it will permanently close the PR. 
9: 
10: Instead, use a hierarchical semantic structure based on the project and the sequential Work Order index:
11: * **Format:** `[project-name]/wo[index]-[topic]`

13:   * `v2-dashboard/wo1-backend-spooler` (Base: `main`)
14:   * `v2-dashboard/wo2-api-routes` (Base: `v2-dashboard/wo1-backend-spooler`)
15:   * `v2-dashboard/wo3-react-ui` (Base: `v2-dashboard/wo2-api-routes`)

17: ### 1.2 Base Resolution: Branch Names, Not Pinned Commits
18: Always declare a Work Order's base as a **branch name** (e.g., `base: main`), never a pinned SHA. When creating a branch, check out from the **live tip of the named base branch at branch-creation time**.
19: 
20: A literal SHA captured when a handoff was *written* goes stale the moment any further commit lands on the base branch — even a docs or ledger commit pushed between handoff authoring and branch creation — silently excluding that commit from the new branch's ancestry.
21: 
22: * **Reading a SHA-pinned handoff:** If a bridge prompt or `PROJECT.md` specifies a literal SHA, interpret it as *"that branch at or after that SHA"* and branch from the current tip — **unless** the handoff explicitly states that later commits must be excluded (e.g., a targeted hotfix cherry-pick).
